title: Contended Shared Writes on High-Frequency Paths
pattern: Multiple cores repeatedly update the same shared counter or status location on a hot path.
why_bad: Every write forces the cache line to change ownership via the coherence protocol; these repeated ownership transfers serialize the updates, waste hundreds of bus cycles on invalidation traffic, and impair multicore scaling.
detection: High-frequency concurrent loops write a shared, non-thread-local location, including global atomic counters updated for every event; distinguish aggregatable statistics (counts, sums) from status state that requires immediately visible coordinated updates.
counterexample: The write is highly sporadic or occurs only on initialization (e.g., a counter merged once per second rather than on every network call); or there is a demonstrated need for immediate shared coordination where delayed aggregation would change semantics. `Contextual`.
source: *Herlihy - Art of Multiprocessor Programming*, Appendix B (p. 476 / p. 138-139) and *1701.00854v6.pdf*, Chapter 3 (p. 25); Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Section 11.3, p. 184.
